newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia plans overhaul of farm machinery.
newsitem.headline: Serbia plans overhaul of farm machinery.

text.p: The Serbian government has secured an additional 330 million dinars for a programme to replace outdated agricultural machinery, the Belgrade daily Politika said on Friday.

"The ministries of agriculture and industry were asked to prepare a plan on intensive replacement of agricultural machinery for which 330 million dinars has been secured," the paper quoted Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic as saying.

He said new tractors and combines were already in the fields as a result of an earlier 205 million dinar programme, launched in April, involving the exchange of farm produce such as wheat and corn for agricultural machinery.
The government has provided a financial injection to idle agricultural machinery manufacturers to produce some 2,000 tractors and 150 combines prior to the 1997 harvest.
According to some estimates, the country has some 418,000 tractors, 250,000 multi-cultivators and 24,000 combines and harvesters.

It is estimated to need around 20,000 additional tractors, 16,000-18,000 combines and 25,000-30,000 other pieces of agricultural equipment each year by the year 2000 to return to pre-war 1990 production levels.
Marjanovic said the government has also secured 180 million dinars to upgrade livestock breeding. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
